emily (AE): Hey team — acme is spinning up the Private deploy POC. They asked for a concise list of egress ports we need opened from their corporate proxy to our connector. They also want to allow SSH outbound for model syncs and NTP. Can SRE confirm minimal set?

kyle (SE): Short answer: HTTPS (443) to our control plane endpoints, gRPC/tcp for streaming if they use our connector, SSH (22) only to a customer-managed bastion if they insist, and NTP (123 UDP) for accurate timestamps. We prefer no inbound SSH to our infra.

nina (NetEng): Agree. From the Private deploy side the concrete egress allowlist we ask customers to permit:
```
TCP 443 -> *.redwood-inference.com (control plane, auth, telemetry)
TCP 443 -> models.redwood-inference.com (model pulls)
TCP 22 -> customer-bastion.example.com:22 (optional, customer-managed)
UDP 123 -> 0.pool.ntp.org (or customer NTP)
TCP 2379 -> internal etcd (not exposed; do NOT allow)
```
Note: we never ask customers to open 2379; just calling that out because it comes up.

omar (Security): A few security constraints to highlight for the questionnaire:
- No persistent inbound management ports on customer VPCs for Redwood.
- We support mTLS on the connector; if you enable it, provide us with the CA thumbprint and SANs.
- For SSH-based model sync, require MFA jump host and audit logging.

emily (AE): Acme asked about IP vs FQDN allowlists — they only allow IP CIDR in their corporate FW. How do we handle model host IP churn?

kyle (SE): We can provide a CIDR block for egress (a set of static ranges) for Dedicated customers. For Hosted-ish Private deployments we give a short list of static egress IPs that are stable for the lifetime of the POC (we rotate on scheduled maintenance windows). We'll include a note in the SOW about planned rotations and lead time.

acme_admin: FYI — security team requires NTP to be pinned to our internal NTP pool (10.10.10.0/24). Is that fine? Also want to allow outbound SSH 22 to our bastion only.

nina (NetEng): That's fine. If NTP is internal, just point the connector to the internal NTP server; we don't need public NTP. For SSH: ensure bastion has strict host keys and we only allow egress to that single IP. Example firewall rule we recommend on the customer side:
```
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 54.123.45.67 port 443 comment "redwood control plane"
allow udp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 10.10.10.0/24 port 123 comment "internal ntp"
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 203.0.113.4 port 22 comment "customer bastion only"
```

omar (Security): Add: please enable TLS 1.2+ and prefer 1.3. Disable RSA < 2048. If customer will do FIPS/HSM, call out KMS integration separately in the security questionnaire.

emily (AE): Pricing question from Acme: will extra SSH model syncs or frequent model pulls increase costs? They may do nightly model refreshes.

kyle (SE): Model pulls are billed as egress/transfer only (tiny). The primary cost driver is inference usage (token counts / dedicated capacity). Nightly pulls are fine — we recommend delta-only syncs or rsync-like transfers. If they want high-frequency syncs during the POC, we can include a temporary storage/bandwidth estimate in the quote.

acme_admin: One last ask — can you provide a short checklist we can hand to our NetOps team?

nina (NetEng): Sending a compact checklist now:
1) Allow outbound TCP 443 to provided IP ranges/FQDNs
2) If using SSH model sync, allow TCP 22 to customer bastion IP only
3) Point connector to internal NTP (UDP 123) or allow UDP 123 to our pool
4) Whitelist CA fingerprints for mTLS if enabled
5) Ensure egress MTU >= 1400 for large model artifacts; test with `curl`/`scp`
6) Provide CIDR for source NAT so we can pin egress IPs in the connector

emily (AE): Perfect — i'll packet this into the POC handoff and add the note about scheduled IP rotations. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
